title: Hand-Held Cut-Off Saws: Control Kickback and Silica Dust
summary: Hand-held cut-off saws are powerful tools. If the blade pinches or binds, the saw can kick back toward you. They also throw sparks, debris, noise, and silica dust. Know the hazards and control each one before you cut.
talking_points: Read the manufacturer's manual for the exact saw you are using. Each saw is different.
Use the right blade for the material and follow the blade and guard specs. Never use the saw without the blade guard or above the maximum speed marked on the blade.
Inspect the saw and blade before use. Look for a warped or damaged blade and a guard that does not work. Tag out any saw with missing or broken parts, including a broken wet-cutting system.
After mounting a new blade, test it at normal speed for 30 seconds with the guard in place before you cut.
Know the three reactive forces: pull-away, climbing, and rotational kickback. Kickback is the most dangerous. It happens when the blade jerks up and back toward you.

Prevent pinching. Do not jam or wedge the blade. Do not push sideways on the blade. Support and secure the material so it cannot fall, pinch the blade, or crush a worker. Use extreme caution when re-entering a cut.
Keep a firm grip with both hands, good balance, and solid footing. Keep all body parts away from the blade. Do not let the blade overheat, because heat can warp it and cause kickback.
Never use a hand-held saw overhead or on a ladder or stepstool. If you must cut at height, use a scissor lift, scaffold, or other elevated work platform.
Control silica dust. Use integrated water delivery or dust collection as OSHA's silica standard (Table 1) requires, and use respiratory protection when it is required.
Check for gas or electric lines in the cutting zone. Clear combustibles away because the saw makes sparks. Let a gas saw cool before refueling.

Wear fitted PPE: hard hat, safety glasses or face shield, hearing protection, cut-resistant gloves, safety shoes, and a respirator when required. Do not wear loose clothing that can catch in the blade.
Make sure the saw cannot start by accident when you change blades. Unplug it or remove the battery. For gas saws, remove the spark plug wire or use the run safety switch.
site_hazards_to_check: Missing, damaged, or non-working blade guards
Warped, cracked, or wrong blades for the material
No water feed or dust collection on the saw when cutting concrete, block, or brick
Gas-powered saws used in basements, vaults, pipes, or other poorly ventilated spaces (carbon monoxide)
Combustible material near the cutting area
Unsupported material that can shift, fall, or pinch the blade
Gas or electric lines embedded in the cut zone
Other workers standing near the cut without eye, face, and hearing protection
